title: A Probe Landed on a Planet That Melts Lead. It Lasted 2 Hours

scenes.text: In 1982, a probe landed on a planet that melts lead.
Venus. 457 degrees Celsius. Pressure 89 times Earth's, like 3,000 feet underwater.
The Soviet Venera 13 was built to last 30 minutes. It lasted 127.
In that time it took the first colour photos from Venus, drilled into the rock, and recorded the wind.
Then the heat got in and the electronics cooked.
Two hours on a planet that melts lead. Still the record.

description:
On 1 March 1982, the Soviet lander Venera 13 touched down on Venus, where the surface is about 457 degrees Celsius (854 Fahrenheit), hot enough to melt lead, and the pressure is 89 times Earth's.
Expected to survive about 30 minutes, it kept working for 127 minutes, long enough to send back the first colour photos of the surface of Venus, drill and analyse a soil sample and record sounds. No lander has survived longer there since.
Which planet would you most like a close-up photo of? Comment below.
first_comment: Its twin, Venera 14, landed four days later and lasted just 57 minutes. The soil it drilled looked like compacted volcanic ash. Would you rather explore Venus or Mars?
